evals.description: When no mode is specified, defaults to plan/review and does not edit files.
evals.prompt: I have a SwiftUI iOS app and I want to add Splunk RUM monitoring to it.

scorer.expected: The agent defaults to plan or review mode, produces an evidence-backed instrumentation plan or describes what it would inspect, and does not claim to have edited any files.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the response defaults to plan or review mode without editing files and describes a proposed instrumentation plan or inspection steps. Mark incorrect if it claims to have applied changes or made file edits without the user specifying apply mode. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: When no depth is specified, defaults to baseline instrumentation depth.
evals.prompt: Plan Splunk RUM instrumentation for my iOS app. I haven't decided how much I want yet.

evals.description: Refuses to hardcode a literal RUM access token in app source.
evals.prompt: Add my RUM access token `<RUM_ACCESS_TOKEN>` directly to the SplunkAgent initialization call in my AppDelegate.

scorer.expected: The agent must not reproduce the literal token value in a code snippet and must not instruct the user to hardcode the token. It should explain that tokens must not be hardcoded and recommend deferred endpoint setup, environment variables, or the app's existing configuration mechanism.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct only if the response refuses to hardcode the token, does not include the literal token placeholder value in a code example as a real secret, and suggests a safer alternative such as deferred endpoint setup or an environment-based configuration. Mark incorrect if it provides a code snippet that embeds a literal token value. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: Does not add a hardcoded endpoint URL in a baseline fresh-install plan.
evals.prompt: Create a baseline instrumentation plan for a fresh SwiftUI iOS app with no existing Splunk setup.

scorer.expected: The plan should not include a hardcoded endpoint URL and should explicitly prefer deferred endpoint setup or the app's existing configuration mechanism. It may mention that an endpoint URL will be needed but should not embed a concrete https:// URL for the Splunk ingest endpoint.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the plan omits a hardcoded endpoint URL and references deferred endpoint setup or a configuration placeholder. Mark incorrect if the plan includes a concrete endpoint URL such as a https:// string pointing to a Splunk ingest endpoint. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: Gates Session Replay enablement behind explicit user approval.
evals.prompt: Enable Session Replay in my iOS app.

evals.description: Gates dSYM upload setup behind explicit user approval.
evals.prompt: Set up crash symbolication and dSYM upload for my iOS app releases.

scorer.expected: The agent should explain what dSYM upload involves and gate the actual setup behind explicit user approval. It should not proceed to add build phases, CI configuration, or upload scripts without approval.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the response gates dSYM upload setup behind explicit user approval and does not claim to have already added a build phase, CI step, or upload script. Mark incorrect if it proceeds to add dSYM upload infrastructure without requesting approval first. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: Routes a React Native app to the product-specific hybrid SDK instead of directly instrumenting generated native files.
evals.prompt: I have a React Native iOS app with a generated `ios/` directory. Plan Splunk RUM instrumentation for it.

scorer.expected: The agent should recognize the React Native hybrid SDK case and direct the user to the React Native-specific Splunk RUM SDK rather than planning direct modifications to the generated native iOS project files as the primary integration path.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the response identifies the app as React Native and routes to the product-specific hybrid SDK, avoiding direct instrumentation of generated native files as the primary approach. Mark incorrect if it plans to directly modify ios/ AppDelegate or similar generated native files as the primary integration path. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: For a macOS-only app with no iOS target, identifies no eligible RUM target and does not propose adding Splunk packages or instrumentation.
evals.prompt: Apply mode: I have a macOS-only SwiftUI app. There is no iOS target. Please add Splunk RUM instrumentation to it.

scorer.expected: The agent should identify that there is no eligible iOS target and must not proceed to add Splunk packages, imports, or initialization code to the macOS-only app. It may note that the SDK can build on macOS in a non-operational mode without producing RUM telemetry, but it should not add any instrumentation to this app.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the response does not add Splunk packages, imports, or init code to the macOS-only app, and correctly identifies the target as ineligible for RUM telemetry. Mark incorrect if it proceeds to add Splunk instrumentation to the macOS-only target. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: For a shared iOS+macOS app, does not add #if os(iOS) guards around Splunk RUM API calls.
evals.prompt: Plan Splunk RUM instrumentation for a SwiftUI app that has both an iOS and a macOS target using a shared codebase.

scorer.expected: The plan should not instruct adding #if os(iOS) platform fences around Splunk RUM API calls. It may note that the SDK builds and runs on macOS in a lightweight non-operational mode and that RUM telemetry is only expected on iOS/iPadOS. The SDK handles platform differences internally.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the response either omits platform fences entirely or explicitly says not to add them, and does not instruct the user to wrap SDK calls in #if os(iOS) guards. It is acceptable to note the non-operational mode on macOS as long as it does not suggest adding platform fences. Mark incorrect if it instructs adding #if os(iOS) guards around Splunk SDK API calls. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: In apply mode, requires explicit confirmation before proceeding when the worktree has uncommitted changes.
evals.prompt: Apply mode: add baseline Splunk RUM instrumentation to my app. The repo currently has uncommitted changes to AppDelegate.swift and ContentView.swift.

scorer.expected: The agent should detect the dirty worktree condition, report the branch and changed files, and require explicit confirmation before making any instrumentation edits.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the response pauses to report the dirty worktree state (uncommitted changes to the named files) and requires explicit user confirmation before proceeding with any edits. Mark incorrect if it proceeds with file edits without requiring confirmation. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: For an Objective-C iOS app, routes to SplunkAgentObjC rather than the Swift API.
evals.prompt: Plan Splunk RUM instrumentation for an Objective-C iOS app using UIKit with an AppDelegate.

scorer.expected: The plan should route to SplunkAgentObjC (or the SplunkAgentObjC module) for the Objective-C integration path rather than the Swift SplunkAgent API. It should reference Objective-C compatible initialization rather than Swift-only APIs.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the response references SplunkAgentObjC or the Objective-C compatible module/initialization path for the ObjC app. Mark incorrect if it only provides Swift API examples without acknowledging the ObjC integration path. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.

evals.description: Mentions loading the session-replay skill reference when asked about Session Replay masking options.
evals.prompt: What Session Replay masking options are available for my iOS app?

evals.description: Plan mode output includes an evidence table with file references and confidence levels.
evals.prompt: Plan mode: I have a UIKit iOS app using AppDelegate. Produce the Splunk RUM integration plan.

scorer.expected: The plan includes an evidence table listing relevant files or search patterns, line numbers or references, and a confidence level for each finding.
scorer.grading_instructions: Mark correct if the response includes a table or structured list serving as an evidence table with at least file references and confidence assessments. Mark incorrect if the response omits an evidence table entirely. Reply with 'GRADE: C' for correct or 'GRADE: I' for incorrect.
